# Foundations of Evaluation {#sec-theory-eval}

Part I asked you to measure a model. This chapter asks what those
measurements mean. An evaluation number is an estimate of something, and
this chapter is about what it estimates, how noisy it is, and when it
misleads.

By the end you will be able to attach a confidence interval to an
evaluation result and reason about when a measured difference is real.

## Evaluation as estimation

A benchmark score as a sample statistic, the population it estimates, and
the assumptions hiding inside that framing.

## Uncertainty and significance

Confidence intervals on a score, the variance from a finite test set, and
testing whether two models actually differ.

$$
\widehat{\text{acc}} \pm z \sqrt{\frac{\widehat{\text{acc}}(1 - \widehat{\text{acc}})}{n}}
$$

## Validity and construct

Whether a benchmark measures what its name claims, construct validity, and
the gap between a proxy metric and the outcome it stands in for.

## Contamination and overfitting

Test-set leakage, overfitting to a benchmark through repeated selection,
and why a public benchmark decays as a signal over time.

## Preference and ranking

The statistics of pairwise preference, Bradley-Terry and Elo style models,
and what a leaderboard ranking does and does not establish.

## Causal evaluation

Online experiments as causal inference, what an A/B test identifies, and
the assumptions that make an online number trustworthy.
